## 1. Claim, scope and criteria

Claim to test: the selected concern/action workflow preserves authority and missing-evidence holds. This protocol tests original ORR-REQ-GEN-001–008, not ISO conformity, legal compliance or plant competence. Identify actual organization, period, records and selected requirement IDs before execution.

## 2. Assessor competence and independence

Record actual assessor, relevant competence, scope and conflicts. Author desk checking is not independent review. A person must not be labelled independent merely because a role title says auditor. Actual intended-user observations and technical specialist decisions are separate evidence classes.

## 3. Method and evidence

Select an ordinary route, a changed-scope route and a missing-outcome-evidence route; record why these samples suit the claim and what remains unsampled. Pin exact forms/criteria/record revisions. For each, trace intake owner, decision authority, acknowledgment, implementation evidence, outcome review and final disposition. Record actual response/observation, source, date, assistance, evidence limitations and finding. Do not invent elapsed time or a result when a task was not run.

## 4. Decision and hold rules

Use supported within scope, unsupported, uncertain, or not run. Missing consequential authority, criteria or evidence prevents a supported conclusion. A completed action without sufficient outcome evidence must retain an open/held disposition. Failures require owner, correction, exact changed version and retest; preserve the failed attempt. A few successful samples do not establish every process or duty.

## 5. Reporting, follow-up and records

Report criteria, sampling, competence/conflicts, exact evidence, freshness, confidence/limits and unresolved findings. Legitimate authority decides acceptance separately from the assessor. Keep actual records privately; only fictional demonstrations enter this library. No fixed retention period or guarantee is supplied. r01: original protocol, not an executed assurance activity.
